content: Older adults diagnosed with diabetes are at an elevated risk of developing cognitive impairments, which may include memory deficits, difficulties with executive functioning, and an increased likelihood of dementia. Chronic hyperglycemia and prolonged duration of diabetes are strongly associated with a progressive decline in cognitive abilities. Screening for cognitive impairment in this population should include concise evaluation tools, such as the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), to identify individuals who may require more detailed neuropsychological assessments. Cognitive impairments can significantly hinder a patient’s ability to perform essential diabetes self-management tasks, such as adhering to medication regimens, maintaining an appropriate diet, and effectively monitoring blood glucose levels, thereby increasing the risk of adverse outcomes like hypoglycemia.
